spots.line: The square is worn flat by market days.
Somebody has stacked firewood against the wall.
The pond is still, and something moves under it.

chests.line: A strongbox behind the firewood, and the lock already broken.
Somebody buried a jar under the fence and did not come back for it.

props.name: the well
props.line: A good deep well. Somebody has carved a fish on the bucket.

props.name: the signpost
props.line: North: the square. South: the ford. Someone has added, underneath: and mind the goose.

props.name: the bread oven
props.line: Still warm. Somebody baked this morning, and has already sold out.

props.name: a smooth grey stone
props.line: A smooth grey stone, half buried at the water's edge.
props.found_line: That will be Wat's lucky stone.

buildings.name: the reeve's house
shut: Somebody inside says they are out.
The reeve keeps a dog. You hear it think about you.

buildings.name: Hesk's house
buildings.shut: Locked. Hesk is at the stall, and the stall is where Hesk's money is.

buildings.name: the chandler's
shut: Closed. A note on the door: BACK WHEN BACK.
Through the round window: candles, and nobody to sell them.

buildings.name: the weaver's cottage
buildings.shut: A loom clacks on the other side of the door, and does not stop for you.

buildings.name: the old mill house
buildings.shut: Flour on the step, and the door barred from the inside.

buildings.name: the burnt house
buildings.shut: The door is warped shut. The smell of the fire never quite left.

people.name: Mirel the Guild Clerk
chatter: A ford village with a Guild board. We are moving up in the world.
Nobody here has shut a gate. Nobody here has had to.

people.name: Wat the Village Idiot
chatter: I counted the geese twice and got a different answer twice.
Steward says stand somewhere else. I've stood everywhere else.
You've got the good boots and all.

hello: Oh! A person. I was hoping it'd be a person.
Hello! I'm Wat. Everybody knows that already, but I like saying it.
again: You came back! Nobody comes back.
It's you again. Good. I'd started to worry you were a dream.

ask.a: Eels. And something that eats eels. And something that eats THAT, but I've only heard it.
Alder. He's the steward. He says 'Wat, stand somewhere else.' I've stood everywhere else.
The fox has a hat now. Before, it didn't. Think about that.

job.ask: You look like you've lost something.
job.offer: My lucky stone. Smooth, grey, about yay big. I dropped it by the pond, skipping the other stones. Which was a mistake, now I think about it.
job.accept: I'll keep an eye out for it.
job.thanks: You're the best person I've ever met. Today.
job.waiting: Did you find it? Is it still lucky?
job.done: That's it! That's the one! ...It's warmer than I remember. Here. I found this in a goose. Don't ask which goose.

people.name: a fox in a stolen hat
chatter: It looks at your purse the way you look at a river you have to cross.
Nobody in the village will say whose hat that was.

text: The fox looks at you, then at your purse, then pointedly away.
The fox yawns, very wide, so you can see all of its teeth.
refuse.won: The coin vanishes. The fox sits, and waits, and seems to expect a question.

talk.hello: The fox tilts the hat at you. It is, somehow, a greeting.

ask.a: The fox adjusts the hat. It is the fox's hat now, the look says, and that is the end of it.
Its tail flicks towards the woodpile, then towards the fence by the meadow. Then it pretends it did nothing of the kind.

talk.bye: The fox is already looking at someone else's purse.

people.name: Grist the Caterpillar
chatter: Eight boots. Eight. You try affording that on a farm wage.
The firewood stacks itself if you have enough hands, and I do.

people.name: a dove that will not settle
chatter: It burns where it lands, and it never lands twice in the same place.

people.name: Hesk the Stallholder

hello: Fresh this morning! Most of it.
Buying or browsing? Browsing's free. Buying's better.

ask.a: The cheese. The cheese is always good. The bread is good on Tuesdays.
Market day it's elbows and geese. Today it's you.

talk.shop: Bread, cheese, apples. A draught or two for the road. Coin first, mind.
talk.bye: Come back market day. Bring friends. Bring their money.

chatter: Bread! Cheese! Bread and cheese!
Fresh this morning. Mostly.

people.name: Dunmore the Smith

refuse.text: Hammer's hot. Come back when it isn't.
refuse.check_q: Let me work the bellows while we talk.
refuse.won: ...Hm. You've done that before. Fine. What do you need?
refuse.still_no: You'll have the eyebrows off us both. Later.

hello: If it's iron, I can make it. If it's not, I can make it iron.

ask.a: I can fix most things. Blades, hinges, marriages. Not that last one. Not twice.

ask.q: Where does the iron come from?
ask.a: Up the pass, past the pine camp. The woodcutters bring it down when the gates let them.

talk.shop: Good honest iron. None of your shine.
talk.sold: It'll outlast you. Try not to prove me wrong.

chatter: Tink. Tink. Tink.
Who left the tongs in the trough?

hello: Bram. I keep this road. Nobody asked me to.
You walk like you've been on the road a while. So have I.
again: Still here. The road's still here too.
Any word of riders out of the broken hills?

ask.a: Master Kaelen's. He put me in the cellar under the quench tank and went back up. I came out. He didn't.

ask.q: What's the scar on your arm?
ask.a: A promise. Cold iron, so it would stay. I find the Iron Hand, every one of them, and I put them in the ground.
An archer and a hedge priest walked with me a while. Sera's in the old grove. Toln's reading in the hall by the hills. We'll be needed together again.

bye: Keep your oaths. They're all you get to keep.

people.name: Maud the Farmer
chatter: Turnips. Again.
If the rain holds off, we eat.

rounds.line: Pulls the weeds out of the planter.
Takes an armful of logs off the pile.
Feeds the logs to the bread oven.
Sets a basket of turnips down at the stall.

people.name: Old Henne
chatter: I remember when this wall was a fence.
Nobody used to lock anything.

rounds.line: Draws a bucket from the well.
Sits a while on the step.
Throws crusts at the pond for the ducks.

people.name: Tamsin the Alewife
chatter: The Crown's ale is mine. The Crown's name is his.

rounds.line: Rolls a barrel off the stack.
Heaves it in at the Ford and Crown's door.
Draws water for the next brew.

people.name: Garrow the Gatewarden
chatter: Gate shuts at dark. Mostly.
Walls keep the wolves out. And the neighbours in.

rounds.line: Walks the inside of the wall.
Checks the far corner for gaps.
